subject: Retainer overlay and fallback credit framework
messages:
From: Sarah Cole <sarah@cloudly.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@cloudly.com
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA packaging — retainer / failover credits question

Jonas —

Thanks for the call today. Quick follow-up from our side: we like the idea of a retainer to guarantee priority handling, but our procurement and platform teams are worried about how credits for cross-region failover and escalation handoffs would be applied.

Questions we need answered to move to legal:
- How are failover credits calculated when we route traffic to a secondary region (per-hour or per-incident)?
- Can retainer dollars be applied as a discount to monthly committed capacity vs only as incident credits?
- What does the escalation coverage look like for 24/7 incidents vs standard business-hour P1s?

I've copied procurement so they can weigh in on contract redlines. If you can send an overlay doc with the crediting model and an example invoice amortization, that would help.

—Sarah
Head of Platform, Cloudly

On Mon, 02 Nov 2026 at 08:00, jonas_weber@redwood.ai wrote:
> Thanks for your time earlier — attaching the high-level retainer overlay that maps to our failover credit matrix.
> 
> I can send a worked example for a $40k/year retainer showing amortization against committed capacity and incident crediting; flag if you'd prefer a seat-based retainer instead of dollars.
>
> Jonas
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Cole <sarah@cloudly.com>
Cc: procurement@cloudly.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Retainer overlay and failover-credit matrix (attached)

Sarah / team —

Attached: redwood-retainer-overlay-v2.pdf and failure-credit-matrix.xlsx. TL;DR on the model so procurement can quickly pick a line item:

1) Failover credits: calculated per-incident and tiered by duration. Small failovers (<30m) = 10% credit of incident-impacted tokens; sustained failovers (>3h) = 50% credit, with a stepped curve in between. Credits are additive up to the retainer cap.

2) Retainer usage: retainer dollars can be used in two ways — (A) as monthly amortized discount against committed capacity (preferred for predictable spend), or (B) as a pool for incident credits (preferred if you want a safety buffer). We can flip the allocation quarterly.

3) Escalation coverage: retainer level maps to on-call tiers. Our standard retainer gives business-hours P1 escalation to our L2/ops team with 4h SLA for triage; premium retainer provides 24/7 L2+L3 coverage with 60m triage and 4h remediation target for infra-layer incidents.

Notes / concessions we can offer for this deal: 10% discount on list retainer if Cloudly commits to 12 months and buys a minimum of 2 regional failover licenses. Also willing to add a canary fallback clause — if your canary fails 3x in a rolling 30d window, we automatically enable priority routing for the remainder of the month at no extra cost.

Ask: can procurement confirm whether they prefer (A) amortized-discount or (B) incident-pool? If (A), I'll drop a worked invoice showing amortization. If (B) we can show a sample incident-runbook.

Thanks — attaching the files now.

—Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: procurement@cloudly.com <procurement@cloudly.com>

Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Retainer overlay and failover-credit matrix (attached)

Jonas —

Procurement here. Quick clarifications from legal/finance after an internal review:
- We need a firm definiton of 'incident-impacted tokens' for credit calculation. Is it based on request count, token count, or a blended metric?
- Can credits be carried forward up to 6 months if unused? Finance prefers carry-forward to avoid losing value.
- For the amortized discount option, we need an example amortization schedule on a monthly invoice that shows the retainer reducing committed capacity line items.

If you can send a 1-page addendum with the definitions + 2 example invoices (one for amortized-discount, one for incident-pool usage) we can expedite legal review.

Procurement point: Maya Patel (finance) may reach out for a short call.

—Cloudly Procurement
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: procurement@cloudly.com, Sarah Cole <sarah@cloudly.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 16:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Retainer overlay and failover-credit matrix (attached)

Thanks for the detailed asks — quick answers and next steps below. Attaching the two worked invoices as requested (amortized-example-invoice.pdf, incident-pool-invoice.pdf).

- 'Incident-impacted tokens': we measure credits by token-equivalent units (TEUs) — a blended metric that normalizes requests by token consumption and inference cost (token count * model-cost-weight). This is the same unit we use in billing so it maps directly to invoice line items.

- Carry-forward: yes, credits can carry forward up to 6 months, but any carried credits applied to an incident will be debited from oldest-first. We cap carry-forwarded credits at the retainer amount to avoid perpetual accumulation.

- Amortization example: the attached amortized-example-invoice.pdf shows a $40k annual retainer applied as a $3,333/month discount against the 'Committed Inference Capacity' line. The incident-pool example shows a $40k pool that is decremented per incident using the failure-credit-matrix.xlsx rules.

Concessions for signature: we can lock in the 10% retainer discount if Cloudly signs within two weeks and commits to the 12-month term + 2 regional failover licenses. I'll follow up to schedule a 30-min call to walk procurement/legal through the addendum.

If Maya wants to chat, she can grab 10a or 2p PT Monday.

—Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: amortized-example-invoice.pdf; incident-pool-invoice.pdf
